title: The Rigged Compass: Panel Banks Bent the World's Reference Rate to Profit Their Own Swap Books

extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: Daily basis-point shifts in LIBOR fixings, requested by derivatives traders at panel banks, moved payouts on interest-rate-swap and other positions priced off the benchmark — a continuous skim across hundreds of trillions in notional instruments.
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: LIBOR was set not from actual transactions but from submissions by the very banks that traded against it, administered by the British Bankers' Association — a self-polled benchmark with no independent verification, constructed for capture.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: Rigging ran through chat rooms, broker intermediaries and oral requests off any transaction record; the absence of an observable market rate meant the manipulation left no direct pricing trail for counterparties to detect.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: Panel banks held privileged knowledge of their own submissions and positions, harvesting gains on swap books and — during 2008 — lower perceived funding costs by lowballing submissions to appear healthier.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: Regulators collected fines (Barclays ~£290m, UBS $1.5bn, RBS ~$612m), a single trader (Tom Hayes) was convicted, and the consolidated private antitrust suit was dismissed at the pleading stage with the Second Circuit affirming in May 2016 — no bank-level criminal conviction on the rate rigging, and the benchmark was quietly re-homed to ICE in 2014.

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: The Thatcher-era Big Bang architecture left benchmark construction to the British Bankers' Association and a submission panel of the same banks that traded on the rate — self-regulation inherited from the 1986 settlement of LIBOR administration.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 criminalised benchmark manipulation and transferred LIBOR to ICE Benchmark Administration — formalising the benchmark while leaving the dealer-panel structure and derivative pricing power intact.
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: Fines and settlement payments flowed to treasuries and regulators, not to the counterparties, municipalities, and borrowers whose student loans, mortgages and municipal swaps were priced off the rigged rate; the derivative gains stayed on bank books.
closedLoopRatchet.enablesNextDossier: The dismissal of antitrust injury claims pushed benchmark-rigging claims into commodity and fraud theories, narrowing private enforcement and hardening the pleading-stage shield later deployed across FX-rigging and other benchmark scandals.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: Regulators (the Fed / Bank of England) ordered the low submissions in 2008, so the whole scandal was official policy and no one was defrauded.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: The pre-2008 profit-driven rigging is documented independently in DOJ settlement statements and the court record; regulator awareness of crisis-period lowballing is a separate, narrower fact that cannot explain seven years of trader-directed fixings.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: Extraction ran through the derivative books — panel banks moved the world's reference rate to win their own swaps, with UBS, RBS and Barclays settlements and the Tom Hayes conviction on the record.
